A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DADP research work. All 18 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E, support a reliable comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original MuJoCo and Adroit policy evaluations, representation-quality measurements, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical experiments and reports revised DADP performance estimates in Table 1.

M1.justification: Sections 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same lagged-context representation learning, representation-biased diffusion prior, and composite prediction objective. Equation 7 merely makes the already-defined context index explicit.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four MuJoCo environments, Adroit Door and Relocate tasks, IID/OOD scenarios, and additional Meta-DT task coverage in Table 3.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CORRO, Prompt-DT, Meta-DT, and the Expert reference. Table 4 retains the same end-to-end, conditional, Mixed DDIM, and supervised comparison variants.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B retain the same domain splits, zero-shot evaluation procedures, model configurations, training budgets, and evaluation episode counts. The revised scores are not accompanied by a reported protocol change.

E4.justification: The temporal-offset, representation-utilization, and mastery analyses in Section 5.3 are unchanged. Appendices C and D retain the same guidance-scale and context-source ablations, representation visualizations, and gait case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report Table 1 results as mean ± standard deviation across five random seeds. Standard-deviation values change, but run-count disclosures and uncertainty-reporting procedures do not.

E6.justification: All 12 DADP mean-and-standard-deviation entries in Table 1 change under unchanged reported settings. For example, HalfCheetah IID changes from 4100 ± 85 to 3978 ± 66, Walker2d OOD from 3015 ± 207 to 2834 ± 285, and Door OOD from 1430 ± 99 to 1494 ± 81. Comparator scores and rankings remain unchanged, as do the other result tables and figures.

T1.justification: Equation 7 replaces the encoder argument τ with τ_{t−Δt}, matching the context already defined immediately below it. This is a notation clarification; the mathematical reasoning, diffusion derivations, and Appendix A toy-case analysis remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about unsupervised representation learning, diffusion modulation, zero-shot adaptation, and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations of representation quality, diffusion utilization, and generalization are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same stationary-dynamics limitation and discussion of extending the approach to non-stationary environments.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same dataset-generation details, baseline adaptations, architectures, and hyperparameters; Appendix E retains identical pseudocode. The code/dataset release statements and project website destination are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to prior representation-learning and domain-adaptive policy methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Pengcheng Wang and Qinghang Liu to the correspondence block, updates the version/date text, and clarifies the context subscript in Equation 7. The prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded correspondence footnote causes localized first-page reflow, including a small shift of the abstract. Figures, captions, table structures, and appendix layouts remain unchanged; Table 1 only receives numerical replacements.

improvement.justification: Equation 7 gains a small clarity improvement, but the quality effect of the unexplained score revisions is uncertain. Walker2d OOD agrees at 3015 between Tables 1 and 4 in v1; v2 changes Table 1 to 2834 while retaining 3015 in Table 4. The PDFs do not explain whether the revisions correct errors or reflect separate evaluations, preventing a reliable judgment of their net effect on paper quality.
